scope: two original product P1 findings only

findings.title: Requirement rows resolve paths only indirectly via slice_bindings
findings.issue: PAI.requirements.json rows carry slices/verification_refs/review_roles/human_gate, but expected_paths are reached only through slice_bindings (requirement→slice→path). Traceability chain exists and is checker-enforced, but path binding is not per-row explicit.
findings.fix: Optional: add expected_paths to each requirement row or state the chain contract in the schema; not blocking since check_pai_plan validates slice membership and slice-level paths.

not_verified: check_pai_plan.py was analyzed statically; its claimed exit 0 was not independently reproduced.
Registry internals of PAI-00 and PAI-02..PAI-31 (only extracts supplied) and whether all matrix verification_refs resolve in docs/design/PAI.design.json.
Content quality of the PAI design/ADR deliverables, future test implementations, runtime behaviour, live/SLO evidence and human acceptance — all out of scope and still 'planned'.
Whether the spec markdown SHA and §13.2 bullet extraction match the actual file contents.
verdict.summary: Both original P1s are resolved in the packet. (1) PAI-01 is now doc/ADR-only (allowed_files contain no src/, tests/ or tools/ paths), so runtime code and tools/check_pai_plan.py are outside its edit scope and it cannot edit its own checker; the checker enforces this (rejects src/tests/tools in PAI-01 allowed_files) plus allow/forbidden overlap checks. Since scope is doc-only, the 'doc-only scope or behavioral tests' alternative is satisfied and structural planning verification is proportionate. (2) Fine-grained traceability now exists: 69 exact spec IDs each map to slices (therefore expected_paths), verification_refs, review_roles and a human_gate; SC13.2-01..10 map to slices, synthetic/recovery test nodes, review roles and human evidence; PAI-26 enumerates all 10 scenarios in expected_interfaces and registers the E2E/load test files, with the checker enforcing spec-ID set equality, verbatim §13.2 scenario text, valid refs and PAI-26 registration. No unresolved P0/P1; no STOP_SHIP. Verdict is limited to these two findings — it is not approval of the full programme, implementation, tests, runtime or human acceptance.
